title: Graph-Guided Transfer Learning to Boost the Efficiency of System-Level Optimization of Analog/Mixed-Signal Circuits
problem: System-level optimization of analog/mixed-signal circuits requires expensive iterative circuit simulations; transfer learning has limited applicability across dissimilar architectures.
motivation: Analog circuit design is a labor-intensive optimization bottleneck; faster design automation through knowledge transfer across circuit families can accelerate development.
method: Combines reinforcement learning with graph attention networks (GAT) and a graph similarity detection method to identify electrical trade-offs; transfers learned policies across different circuit topologies by recognizing structural similarities.
key_novelty: Graph similarity detection embedded in transfer learning to enable cross-architecture knowledge transfer for analog circuits.
contributions: 11x reduction in simulation count via transfer learning on analog circuits
12.4% improvement in optimization quality vs. from-scratch baseline
Generalizable framework applicable to broad range of analog/mixed-signal systems
limitations: Case study limited to 4th-order continuous-time Delta-Sigma ADCs.
primary_theme: Transfer learning for analog circuit synthesis
